primary_claim: Linear probes trained on Mistral7B's hidden activations discriminate high- versus low-cyber-risk input scenarios with F1 up to 0.85-0.95 and AUC up to 0.96 in several later layers, and the top neurons identified causally boost cybersecurity-related output tokens.

effect.metric: F1 / AUC of linear probe risk classifier
effect.value: F1 0.85-0.95; AUC up to 0.96 for several layers

stated_future_work: Finishing to explore the attention patterns of our triggers to explain the circuit (WIP)
Clamping activations on groups of more than 1 neuron to observe output effects.
Visualize activations not at the end of an input but throughout, to search for snap intermediate triggers vs ultimate state.
Training multiple classes of risks and/or a 5 point severity scale (instead of binary classification)
Finding which embedding dimensions have weights correlated highly to the ones learned by the linear probes.
limitations_stated: here, I do not address design/architecture efforts and how they might improve signal/noise tradeoffs
without a budget to train Sparse Autoencoders on holistic corpora, the appeal of working with SAEs looked out of reach
the test on the individual neuron makes a certain difference, but it's not reliable on its own (as evidenced by red herrings from superposition)
quote: found confidence that the model generally senses when something is up in a given input text, vs low risk scenarios (F1>0.85 for 4 layers; AUC in some layers exceeds 0.96)
